content.title: Walkthroughs: explain a PR stack from cited code
content.intent: This stack adds Walkthroughs: a hidden Turn reads a PR stack and submits a story, and Junior checks every citation against the provider before storing it.

chapters.caption: The model cites line ranges and Junior copies the code
chapters.body: A Walkthrough points at evidence: code by PR, path, side, and lines, plus messages, links, or checks [1]. The model never copies code. After the checks pass, Junior builds each excerpt from the provider's diff, or from the head file for code outside the diff [2].
asks: Why not let the model quote code directly?

chapters.caption: The validator rejects unresolved citations and skipped hunks
chapters.body: A base-side range must sit inside one hunk, and a head-side range outside the diff must fit the file at the head commit [1]. Every hunk must overlap a citation unless its file is listed as not covered [2]. Lockfiles, generated files, renames, and whitespace-only edits are dropped before the model sees them [3].

decisions.claim: Path and @generated-marker checks catch enough generated files that the model does not have to cover them.
decisions.concern: Drizzle snapshots under migrations/meta/ do not match, so the 4,652-line 0101_snapshot.json in #3090 reaches the model.

asks: Does a file listed in not_covered still count when a chapter also cites it?

chapters.caption: Core reads code changes only through a provider plugin hook
chapters.body: The plugin API adds CodeChangeHooks: readStack, readDiff, and readFile [1]. Their context carries egress with Junior's system identity, not a user's [2]. Core builds that egress from a system Actor and turns off authorization prompts, then checks each result against a schema [3].
asks: What happens when a provider has no code-change plugin?

chapters.caption: GitHub finds the stack through the Stacks API, then by walking base branches
chapters.body: GitHub first asks the Stacks API, and treats a 404 as no stack support [1]. Without it, GitHub walks open PRs down and up through base branches, and stops where the chain forks [2]. Closed or merged layers are dropped [3], and diffs compare the exact base and head SHAs, so a push during generation does not change them [4].

decisions.claim: GitHub answers 404 whenever a repository cannot use the Stacks API.
decisions.concern: Any other error, such as a 400 for an unknown API version, fails the read instead of falling back to base branches.

decisions.claim: Merged or closed layers drop out of a stack's Walkthrough.
decisions.concern: Someone reviewing the top layer loses the story of a base layer that just merged.

asks: Why per_page=2 when listing parent and child PRs?

chapters.caption: One live version per stack snapshot, so a second click joins the first
chapters.body: A new table holds one row for each generation [1]. A partial unique index on provider, repository, and snapshot key ignores failed rows, so a failure can be retried [2]. The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and falls back to the live row, so two clicks at the same time start only one generation [3].
asks: Why no foreign key from generation_conversation_id to Conversations?

chapters.caption: The migration only adds a table, but every Conversation list gains a subquery
chapters.body: The migration only creates a table and its indexes, so existing rows are untouched. Completing or failing a version only applies while it is still generating [1]. Conversation lists now skip Conversations that a version row names, through a NOT EXISTS subquery [2].

decisions.claim: The NOT EXISTS subquery adds no noticeable cost to Conversation lists and searches.
decisions.concern: It runs for every candidate row. The unique index serves it, but nothing measures it on a large install.

asks: Is dropping the table a safe rollback?

chapters.caption: A generation Turn gets submitWalkthrough and loses tools that reach people
chapters.body: A new Turn behavior turns off agents, the review desk, subscriptions, and noReply, and turns on submitWalkthrough [1]. It wins over every other behavior when the Run is a generation [2]. The tool exists only when the Run also carries the generation it writes [3], and the skill stops when the tool is missing [4].

decisions.claim: A generation Turn can keep the normal sandbox and provider tools for exploring.
decisions.concern: The Turn runs as the person who clicked, so exploration may use their credentials while the submit check uses the system identity.

chapters.caption: submitWalkthrough re-reads the provider and stores only a checked document
chapters.body: The sandbox is not trusted, so the tool reads the diff, the cited head files, and the cited messages again through the plugin [1]. Problems go back to the model as a tool input error so it can retry. Only a clean output becomes a document, and storing it fails if the version is no longer generating [2]. One submission can cite code from at most 30 files [3].
asks: Are diff reads cached across retries in one Turn?

chapters.caption: POST /api/walkthroughs reads the stack, claims a version, and enqueues a hidden Turn
chapters.body: The route hands the provider, repository, and PR number to startWalkthrough, and answers 202 [1]. That function reads the stack, claims the snapshot, and only on a new claim enqueues a public Conversation that runs the skill [2]. A source Conversation comes from the PR footer marker, and only a public one is used [3]. Reads check source access again [4].

decisions.claim: Any signed-in viewer may start a Walkthrough of any repository that the provider plugin can read.
decisions.concern: Reads use Junior's system identity, so a viewer without repo access could read its diffs in the stored document.

decisions.claim: A public generation Conversation is safe because Conversation lists hide it.
decisions.concern: Hidden is not private: anyone with its id may read a transcript that quotes code from a private repository.

asks: What does a viewer see when the source Conversation turns private?

chapters.caption: The Turn worker connects a Conversation to the version it generates
chapters.body: Before each Turn, the worker looks up a generating version for the Conversation [1]. readWalkthroughRun passes the generation into the Run, and its finish step fails the version if no Walkthrough was stored [2]. The worker calls finish after the Run returns [3]. A later click marks generations older than 30 minutes as failed [4].

decisions.claim: A 30-minute timeout is enough to free a snapshot after a crashed generation.
decisions.concern: A Turn that throws skips finish, so the snapshot stays generating until someone clicks again after 30 minutes.

asks: Does every Turn now pay for one extra version lookup?

chapters.caption: Generation Turns run under tighter limits behind the walkthroughs experiment
chapters.body: A generation Turn has a limit of 80 tool calls and $5 [1], and the agent loop now reads these limits from the Turn behavior before the app defaults [2]. Every Walkthrough route returns 404 unless the app turns on the new walkthroughs experiment [3] [4].

decisions.claim: 80 tool calls and $5 are enough to explain a large stack.
decisions.concern: This stack's diffs total about 250 KB, and a Turn that hits a limit fails its version with no partial result.

chapters.caption: Cost and failure reasons on each version show whether generation works
chapters.body: Each version response includes its generation cost and failure reason [1]. Cost is the sum of the generation Conversation's cost_usd metrics [2]. After shipping, watch the failure reasons: timed out, could not start, or the Turn ended without a Walkthrough [3].

decisions.claim: Version rows are enough to tell whether Walkthroughs work after shipping.
decisions.concern: No metric or log counts failures by reason, so a rise in failures shows only when someone queries the table.
